verses.1:1: To the Jewish brothers who are throughout Egypt, the Jewish brothers who are in Jerusalem and those who are in the region of Judea send greetings and good peace.
verses.1:2: May God do good to you, and remember His covenant which He spoke to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, His faithful servants;
verses.1:3: and grant to all of you a heart to worship Him and carry out His will with a great heart and a willing spirit.
verses.1:4: May He open your heart in His law and in His precepts, and make peace.
verses.1:5: May He hear your prayers and be reconciled to you, and not abandon you in an evil time.
verses.1:6: And now we are here praying for you.
verses.1:7: While Demetrius was reigning, in the one hundred sixty-ninth year, we Jews wrote to you in the tribulation and onslaught that came upon us in these years, from the time Jason withdrew from the holy land and from the kingdom.
verses.1:8: They set fire to the gate and shed innocent blood; and we prayed to the Lord, and we were heard, and we offered sacrifice and fine flour, and we lit the lamps, and we set out the loaves.
verses.1:9: And now celebrate the days of Tabernacles of the month of Chislev.
verses.1:10: In the one hundred eighty-eighth year, the people who are in Jerusalem and in Judea, and the senate, and Judas, to Aristobulus, teacher of King Ptolemy, who is of the lineage of the anointed priests, and to the Jews who are in Egypt: greetings and health.
verses.1:11: Having been delivered by God from great dangers, we greatly give thanks to Him, as those who have fought against such a king.
verses.1:12: For He Himself caused those who fought against us and the holy city to pour forth from Persia.
verses.1:13: For when the leader himself was in Persia, and with him an immense army, he fell in the temple of Nanea, deceived by the counsel of the priests of Nanea.
verses.1:14: For Antiochus and his friends came to the place intending to live with her, and so that he might receive large sums of money by way of a dowry.
verses.1:15: And when the priests of Nanea had set them out, and he himself with a few others had entered inside the enclosure of the shrine, they shut the temple,
verses.1:16: once Antiochus had entered; and having opened a hidden entrance of the temple, throwing stones, they struck down the leader and those who were with him, and cut them apart limb by limb, and having cut off their heads, they threw them outside.
verses.1:17: In all things blessed be God, who has handed over the ungodly.
verses.1:18: Therefore, being about to perform the purification of the temple on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Chislev, we considered it necessary to inform you, so that you also may observe the day of Tabernacles and the day of the fire, which was given when Nehemiah, after the temple and the altar had been built, offered sacrifices.
verses.1:19: For when our fathers were being led into Persia, the priests who were then worshipers of God took fire from the altar and secretly hid it in a valley, where there was a deep and dry well, and in it they kept it safely, so that the place was unknown to everyone.
verses.1:20: Now when many years had passed, and it pleased God that Nehemiah should be sent by the king of Persia, he sent the descendants of those priests who had hidden it to search for the fire; and as they reported to us, they did not find fire, but thick water.
verses.1:21: And he commanded them to draw it and bring it to him; and the priest Nehemiah commanded the sacrifices that had been set in place to be sprinkled with that very water, both the wood and the things that were laid on top.
verses.1:22: And when this was done, and the time came when the sun shone forth, which previously was in a cloud, a great fire was kindled, so that all marveled.
verses.1:23: Now all the priests were offering prayer while the sacrifice was being completed, Jonathan beginning and the rest responding.
verses.1:24: And Nehemiah's prayer had this form: "Lord God, Creator of all things, awesome and strong, righteous and merciful, who alone is a good King,
verses.1:25: alone bountiful, alone righteous and almighty and eternal, who deliver Israel from every evil, who made the fathers chosen and sanctified them:
verses.1:26: accept the sacrifice for all Your people Israel, and guard Your portion, and sanctify it.
verses.1:27: Gather our dispersion, deliver those who serve the nations, and look upon the despised and detested, so that the nations may know that You are our God.
verses.1:28: Afflict those who oppress us and who inflict outrage in pride.
verses.1:29: Establish Your people in Your holy place, just as Moses said."
verses.1:30: Meanwhile the priests were singing hymns until the sacrifice was consumed.
verses.1:31: And when the sacrifice had been consumed, Nehemiah commanded that the larger stones be drenched with the remaining water.
verses.1:32: When this was done, a flame was kindled from them; but by the light that shone forth from the altar, it was consumed.
verses.1:33: Now when the matter became known, it was reported to the king of the Persians that in the place in which those priests who had been deported had hidden the fire, water appeared, with which Nehemiah and those who were with him purified the sacrifices.
verses.1:34: And the king, considering and carefully examining the matter, made a temple for it in order to verify what had happened;
verses.1:35: and when he had verified it, he bestowed on the priests many good things and one gift after another, and taking them with his own hand, he distributed them to them.
verses.1:36: Now Nehemiah called this place Nephthar, which is interpreted Purification; but among most people it is called Nephi.
verses.2:1: Now it is found in the records of Jeremiah the prophet that he commanded those who were going into exile to take the fire, as was indicated, and as he charged the exiles.
verses.2:2: And he gave them the law, so that they would not forget the precepts of the Lord and would not go astray in their minds when seeing images of gold and silver and their adornments.
verses.2:3: And saying other things of this kind, he urged them not to remove the law from their heart.
verses.2:4: Now it was in that same writing how the prophet, after a divine response had been given to him, commanded the tabernacle and the ark to accompany him, until he went out to the mountain on which Moses went up and saw the inheritance of God.
verses.2:5: And coming there, Jeremiah found the place of a cave, and he brought the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense in there, and blocked up the entrance.
verses.2:6: And some of those who were following came up together in order to mark the place for themselves, and they were not able to find it.
verses.2:7: Now when Jeremiah learned of this, rebuking them he said, "The place will be unknown until God gathers the assembly of the people and becomes gracious,
verses.2:8: and then the Lord will show these things, and the majesty of the Lord will appear, and there will be a cloud, just as it was also manifested to Moses, and just as when Solomon asked that the place be sanctified to the great God, He manifested these things."
verses.2:9: For indeed he practiced wisdom magnificently; and as one having wisdom, he offered the sacrifice of the dedication and completion of the temple.
verses.2:10: Just as Moses also prayed to the Lord, and fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering, so Solomon also prayed, and fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering.
verses.2:11: And Moses said, "Because what was for sin was not eaten, it was consumed."
verses.2:12: Likewise Solomon also celebrated the dedication for eight days.
verses.2:13: Now these same things were recorded in the records and memoirs of Nehemiah, and how, building a library, he gathered from the regions the books both of the prophets and of David, and letters of kings, and concerning dedicated gifts.
verses.2:14: And likewise Judas also gathered all the things that had been lost through the war that happened to us, and they are with us.
verses.2:15: Therefore, if you desire these things, send those who will bring them to you.
verses.2:16: Accordingly, being about to observe the purification, we have written to you; you will therefore do well if you observe these days.
verses.2:17: Now God, who delivered His people and restored the inheritance to all, and the kingdom, and the priesthood, and the sanctification,
verses.2:18: just as He promised in the law, we hope that He will soon have mercy on us, and He has gathered us from under heaven into the holy place.
verses.2:19: For He has rescued us from great dangers, and has cleansed the place.
verses.2:20: Now concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, and concerning the purification of the great temple, and concerning the dedication of the altar,
verses.2:21: and also concerning the battles that pertain to Antiochus the Noble and his son Eupator,
verses.2:22: and concerning the illuminations that took place from heaven for those who acted bravely for the Jews, so that, though they were few, they reclaimed the entire region and put the barbarian multitude to flight,
verses.2:23: and recovered the most famous temple in the whole world, and delivered the city, and the laws that had been abolished were restored, the Lord having become gracious to them with all tranquility.
verses.2:24: And likewise, what was contained in five books by Jason of Cyrene we have attempted to abridge into one volume.
verses.2:25: For considering the multitude of books, and the difficulty for those wishing to undertake the narratives of the histories because of the multitude of matters,
verses.2:26: we have taken care that for those wishing to read there might be delight of mind, for the studious that they may more easily commit it to memory, and that for all readers benefit may be conferred.
verses.2:27: And for ourselves indeed, who have undertaken this work for the sake of abridging, we have taken on no easy labor, but rather a task full of vigils and sweat.
verses.2:28: Just like those who prepare a banquet and seek to comply with the wish of others, for the sake of the gratitude of many we gladly endure the labor,
verses.2:29: conceding indeed the truth concerning each detail to the authors, while we ourselves strive for brevity according to the given form.
verses.2:30: For just as the architect of a new house must take care of the entire structure, while he who attends to painting must seek out the things that are fitting for adornment, so also must it be judged in our case.
verses.2:31: For indeed to gather the understanding, and to arrange the discourse, and to investigate each individual part more carefully, befits the author of a history;
verses.2:32: but to pursue brevity of expression and to avoid detailed treatments of matters must be conceded to the one who abridges.
verses.2:33: From here, therefore, we will begin the narrative; let it be enough to have said this much concerning the preface. For indeed it is foolish to overflow before the history, yet to be cut short in the history itself.
verses.3:1: Therefore, while the holy city was inhabited in complete peace and the laws also were still kept very well, because of the piety of Onias the high priest and minds that hated evil,
verses.3:2: it came about that even the kings and princes themselves considered the place worthy of the highest honor and glorified the temple with the greatest gifts,
verses.3:3: so that Seleucus, king of Asia, provided from his own revenues all the expenses pertaining to the service of the sacrifices.
verses.3:4: But Simon, of the tribe of Benjamin, who had been appointed overseer of the temple, was striving to contrive something unjust in the city, though the chief of the priests opposed him.
verses.3:5: But when he could not overcome Onias, he came to Apollonius, the son of Tharseas, who at that time was governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia,
verses.3:6: and reported to him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of countless sums of money, and that the public resources were immense, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, and that it was possible for all of it to fall under the power of the king.
verses.3:7: And when Apollonius had brought word to the king about the sums of money that had been reported, he summoned Heliodorus, who was over his affairs, and sent him with orders to transport the aforementioned money.
verses.3:8: And immediately Heliodorus set out on his journey, in appearance indeed as though he were about to travel through the cities across Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, but in reality to carry out the king's purpose.
verses.3:9: But when he had come to Jerusalem and had been kindly received by the high priest in the city, he told about the information that had been given concerning the money, and disclosed for what reason he was present; and he asked whether these things were truly so.
verses.3:10: Then the high priest showed that these were deposits and provisions for widows and orphans;
verses.3:11: that some indeed belonged to Hyrcanus, the son of Tobias, a very eminent man, among the things that the impious Simon had reported; and that in all there were four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold;
verses.3:12: and that it was altogether impossible for those who had trusted in the place and the temple, which is honored throughout the whole world for its reverence and holiness, to be deceived.
verses.3:13: But he, on account of what he had in his orders from the king, kept saying that by all means they had to be delivered to the king.
verses.3:14: Now on the appointed day, Heliodorus went in to make arrangements concerning these matters. And there was no small alarm throughout the whole city.
verses.3:15: And the priests threw themselves down before the altar in their priestly robes and called upon Him from heaven who established the law concerning deposits, that He would keep them safe for those who had deposited them.
verses.3:16: Indeed, whoever saw the expression of the high priest was wounded in mind, for his face and altered color revealed the inward grief of his soul.
verses.3:17: For a certain sadness had enveloped the man, and a shuddering of his body, through which the grief of his heart became evident to those looking on.
verses.3:18: Others also streamed together in throngs from their houses, imploring in public supplication, because the place was about to come into contempt.
verses.3:19: And women, wrapped with sackcloth around their chests, streamed together through the streets; and even the virgins who were kept shut in ran out to Onias, while others ran to the walls, and some looked out through the windows.
verses.3:20: And all of them, stretching out their hands toward heaven, pleaded in prayer;
verses.3:21: for the expectation of the mingled crowd and of the high priest, who stood in agony, was pitiful.
verses.3:22: And they indeed were calling upon Almighty God that the things entrusted to them might be preserved with complete integrity for those who had entrusted them.
verses.3:23: But Heliodorus was carrying out what he had resolved, himself present in that same place with his guards around the treasury.
verses.3:24: But the Spirit of Almighty God made a great display of His manifestation, so that all who had dared to obey him, collapsing by the power of God, were turned into faintness and terror.
verses.3:25: For there appeared to them a certain horse having a terrifying rider, adorned with the finest trappings; and with a violent rush it struck its front hooves against Heliodorus, and the one who sat upon it appeared to have golden armor.
verses.3:26: Two other young men also appeared, distinguished in strength, surpassing in glory, and splendid in attire, who stood around him and flogged him from both sides, beating him without ceasing with many blows.
verses.3:27: And suddenly Heliodorus collapsed to the ground, and they snatched him up, enveloped in thick darkness, and having placed him on a litter, they carried him out.
verses.3:28: And the one who had entered the aforementioned treasury with many runners and guards was being carried, with no one bringing him help, since the manifest power of God had been recognized;
verses.3:29: and he indeed, through divine power, lay mute and deprived of all hope and deliverance.
verses.3:30: But they were blessing the Lord, because He was magnifying His place; and the temple, which a little while before had been full of fear and uproar, was filled with joy and gladness at the appearing of the Almighty Lord.
verses.3:31: Then indeed some of the friends of Heliodorus immediately begged Onias to call upon the Most High, that He would grant life to the one who was at his very last breath.
verses.3:32: Now the high priest, considering that the king might perhaps suspect that some malice had been perpetrated against Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a saving sacrifice for the man's recovery.
verses.3:33: And while the high priest was praying earnestly, the same young men, clothed in the same garments, stood beside Heliodorus and said, "Give thanks to Onias the priest, for on his account the Lord has granted you life.
verses.3:34: And you, having been flogged by God, proclaim to all the great works of God and His power." And when these words had been spoken, they appeared no more.
verses.3:35: Then Heliodorus, having offered a sacrifice to God and promised great vows to Him who granted him to live, and giving thanks to Onias, took back his army and returned to the king.
verses.3:36: And he testified to everyone about the works of the great God that he had seen before his own eyes.
verses.3:37: Now when the king asked Heliodorus who would be suitable to be sent once more to Jerusalem, he said,
verses.3:38: "If you have any enemy or plotter against your kingdom, send him there, and you will receive him back flogged, if indeed he escapes; because there is truly a certain power of God in the place.
verses.3:39: For He Himself, who has His dwelling in the heavens, is the watcher and helper of that place, and He strikes and destroys those who come to do evil."
verses.3:40: Therefore, concerning Heliodorus and the safeguarding of the treasury, this is how the matter stands.
verses.4:1: Now Simon, who was mentioned earlier, the informer concerning the money and his homeland, was speaking evil about Onias, as if he himself had provoked Heliodorus to these things and he himself had been the instigator of the evils,
verses.4:2: and he dared to call the provider for the city, the defender of his own nation, and the zealot for the law of God a plotter against the kingdom.
verses.4:3: But when the hostilities advanced to such a point that murders were even committed through certain close associates of Simon,
verses.4:4: Onias, considering the danger of the strife and that Apollonius, being commander of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, was raging to increase the malice of Simon, went to the king,
verses.4:5: not as an accuser of the citizens, but considering within himself the common benefit of the entire multitude.
verses.4:6: For he saw that without royal oversight it was impossible for peace to be given to affairs, and that Simon could not cease from his folly.
verses.4:7: But after the departure of Seleucus from life, when Antiochus, who was called the Noble, had assumed the kingdom, Jason, the brother of Onias, sought the high priesthood,
verses.4:8: having approached the king, promising him three hundred sixty talents of silver, and from other revenues eighty talents.
verses.4:9: In addition to these, he also promised another one hundred fifty, if it were granted to his authority to establish for himself a gymnasium and a training school for youths, and to enroll those who were in Jerusalem as Antiochenes.
verses.4:10: When the king had consented to this and he had obtained the leadership, he immediately began to bring his fellow tribesmen over to the Gentile custom;
verses.4:11: and having removed those things which had been established for the Jews out of kindness by the kings through John, the father of Eupolemus, who carried out a lawful embassy before the Romans concerning friendship and alliance, abandoning the rights of the citizens, he ratified perverse practices.
verses.4:12: For indeed he dared to establish a gymnasium beneath the citadel itself, and to place all the finest of the youths in brothels.
verses.4:13: Now this was not a beginning, but a certain increase and advance of Gentile and foreign conduct, because of the abominable and unheard-of crime of the impious Jason, who was no priest,
verses.4:14: so that the priests were no longer devoted to the duties of the altar, but having despised the temple and neglected the sacrifices, they hurried to become participants in the wrestling arena and its unjust provision, and in the exercises of the discus.
verses.4:15: And indeed, holding ancestral honors as nothing, they judged Greek glories to be the best,
verses.4:16: for the sake of which a dangerous strife held them, and they emulated their practices, and desired in all things to be altogether like those whom they had held as enemies and destroyers.
verses.4:17: For to act impiously against the divine laws does not go unpunished; but the time that follows will make this clear.
verses.4:18: Now when the five-year contest was being celebrated at Tyre and the king was present,
verses.4:19: the wicked Jason sent sinful men from Jerusalem, carrying three hundred didrachmas of silver for the sacrifice of Hercules, which those who had conveyed them requested should not be spent on sacrifices, because it was not fitting, but that they be assigned to other expenses.
verses.4:20: Yet these were indeed offered for the sacrifice of Hercules by the one who had sent them; because of those who were present, however, they were given for the construction of trireme ships.
verses.4:21: Now after Apollonius, the son of Mnestheus, had been sent into Egypt on account of the leading men of King Ptolemy Philometor, when Antiochus had learned that he had become estranged from the affairs of the kingdom, looking out for his own interests, departing from there he came to Joppa, and from there to Jerusalem.
verses.4:22: And having been magnificently received by Jason and the city, he entered with the lights of torches and with praises; and from there he turned his army into Phoenicia.
verses.4:23: And after a period of three years, Jason sent Menelaus, the brother of the Simon mentioned above, carrying the money to the king and intending to deliver answers concerning necessary affairs.
verses.4:24: But he, having been commended to the king, when he had magnified the appearance of his authority, turned the high priesthood back onto himself, adding three hundred talents of silver above Jason.
verses.4:25: And having received orders from the king, he came, having indeed nothing worthy of the priesthood, but bearing the spirit of a cruel tyrant and the wrath of a wild beast.
verses.4:26: And Jason indeed, who had taken his own brother captive, being himself deceived, was driven out as a fugitive into the Ammonite region.
verses.4:27: Now Menelaus indeed obtained the leadership, but concerning the money promised to the king he did nothing, even while Sostratus, who was placed over the citadel, was demanding collection,
verses.4:28: for to this man belonged the collection of tributes; for which reason both of them were summoned to the king.
verses.4:29: And Menelaus was removed from the priesthood, with his brother Lysimachus succeeding him; Sostratus, however, was placed over the Cyprians.
verses.4:30: And while these things were taking place, it happened that the people of Tarsus and Mallus stirred up an insurrection, because they had been given as a gift to Antiochis, the king's concubine.
verses.4:31: Therefore the king came in haste to calm them, having left Andronicus, one of his companions, as deputy.
verses.4:32: Now Menelaus, supposing that he had received an opportune time, having stolen certain golden vessels from the temple, presented them to Andronicus, and he had sold others at Tyre and throughout the neighboring cities.
verses.4:33: When Onias had learned this with complete certainty, he rebuked him, while keeping himself in a safe place at Antioch beside Daphne.
verses.4:34: Accordingly, Menelaus, approaching Andronicus, asked that he kill Onias. When he had come to Onias, and after giving right hands with an oath (although he was suspected by him) had persuaded him to come out from the sanctuary, he immediately killed him, not fearing justice.
verses.4:35: For this reason not only the Jews, but also the other nations were indignant and were distressed over the unjust murder of so great a man.
verses.4:36: But when the king returned from the regions of Cilicia, the Jews at Antioch approached him, together with the Greeks as well, complaining about the wicked murder of Onias.
verses.4:37: Therefore Antiochus, saddened in spirit on account of Onias and moved to mercy, shed tears, remembering the sobriety and moderation of the deceased;
verses.4:38: and inflamed in spirit, he ordered Andronicus, stripped of his purple robe, to be led around through the entire city, and in the very same place in which he had committed the impiety against Onias, for the sacrilegious man to be deprived of life, with the Lord repaying him a fitting punishment.
verses.4:39: Now when many acts of sacrilege had been committed in the temple by Lysimachus at the counsel of Menelaus, and the report had spread abroad, a multitude gathered together against Lysimachus, much gold having already been carried out.
verses.4:40: Now as the crowds rose up and their spirits were filled with wrath, Lysimachus, having armed nearly three thousand men, began to use wicked hands, with a certain tyrant as leader, advanced equally in age and in madness.
verses.4:41: But when they perceived the attempt of Lysimachus, some seized stones, others stout clubs, and some threw ashes at Lysimachus.
verses.4:42: And indeed many were wounded, and some were even struck down, and all were turned to flight; even the sacrilegious man himself they killed beside the treasury.
verses.4:43: Concerning these things, therefore, a trial began to be conducted against Menelaus.
verses.4:44: And when the king had come to Tyre, three men sent by the elders brought the matter before him.
verses.4:45: And when Menelaus was being overcome, he promised to give Ptolemy much money to persuade the king.
verses.4:46: Therefore Ptolemy approached the king, who was in a certain courtyard as if for the sake of cooling off, and drew him away from his decision;
verses.4:47: and Menelaus indeed, guilty of every malice, he acquitted of the charges; but the wretched men who, even if they had pleaded their case before the Scythians, would have been judged innocent, these he condemned to death.
verses.4:48: Quickly, therefore, they paid an unjust penalty, who had pursued the case on behalf of the city, the people, and the sacred vessels.
verses.4:49: On account of this, the Tyrians also, being indignant, showed themselves most generous regarding their burial.
verses.4:50: Menelaus, however, on account of the greed of those who were in power, remained in authority, growing in malice for plots against the citizens.
verses.5:1: At the same time, Antiochus prepared a second expedition into Egypt.
verses.5:2: Now it happened throughout the entire city of Jerusalem that for forty days there were seen horsemen riding back and forth through the air, wearing gilded robes and armed with spears, like cohorts,
verses.5:3: and charges of horses arranged in ranks, and clashes taking place at close quarters, and movements of shields, and a multitude of helmeted men with drawn swords, and the hurling of missiles, and the gleam of golden armor and of breastplates of every kind.
verses.5:4: Therefore everyone prayed that the portents might be turned to good.
verses.5:5: But when a false rumor had gone out as though Antiochus had departed from life, Jason, taking no fewer than a thousand men, suddenly attacked the city; and while the citizens rushed together to the wall, when the city was at last captured, Menelaus fled into the citadel.
verses.5:6: Jason, however, did not spare his own citizens in the slaughter, nor did he consider that success against kinsmen is the greatest evil, supposing that he was going to capture trophies of enemies and not of citizens.
verses.5:7: And indeed he did not obtain the leadership, but received disgrace as the end of his plots, and as a fugitive he went away again into Ammanitis.
verses.5:8: At last, hemmed in to his own ruin by Aretas, tyrant of the Arabs, fleeing from city to city, hateful to all as a deserter of the laws and detestable as an enemy of his homeland and citizens, he was driven out into Egypt;
verses.5:9: and he who had driven many out of his homeland perished in a foreign land, having set out to the Lacedaemonians as though he would have a refuge there on account of kinship;
verses.5:10: and he who had cast out many unburied was himself cast out both unmourned and unburied, neither receiving a foreign burial nor sharing in an ancestral tomb.
verses.5:11: So when these things had taken place, the king suspected that the Jews were about to abandon the alliance; and because of this, setting out from Egypt with ferocious rage, he captured the city by force of arms.
verses.5:12: And he ordered the soldiers to kill, not to spare those they encountered, and to slaughter those going up through the houses.
verses.5:13: So there took place slaughters of young men and old men, destructions of women and children, and killings of virgins and infants.
verses.5:14: Now in three whole days there were eighty thousand killed, forty thousand bound, and no fewer sold.
verses.5:15: But not even these things are enough: he also dared to enter the temple holier than the whole earth, with Menelaus as his guide, who was a traitor to the laws and his homeland;
verses.5:16: and taking with wicked hands the holy vessels that had been placed by other kings and cities for the adornment and glory of the place, he handled them unworthily and defiled them.
verses.5:17: Thus, beside himself in mind, Antiochus did not consider that because of the sins of those inhabiting the city, God had been angry for a little while, on account of which disregard also came about concerning the place.
verses.5:18: Otherwise, had it not happened that they were entangled in many sins, just like Heliodorus, who was sent by King Seleucus to plunder the treasury, this man too, immediately upon arriving, would certainly have been flogged and driven back from his audacity.
verses.5:19: Yet God did not choose the nation for the sake of the place, but the place for the sake of the nation.
verses.5:20: Therefore the place itself also became a sharer in the evils of the people, but afterward it will become a partner in good things; and that which was abandoned in the wrath of Almighty God will again be exalted with the highest glory in the reconciliation of the great Lord.
verses.5:21: Therefore Antiochus, having carried off one thousand eight hundred talents from the temple, swiftly returned to Antioch, imagining in his pride that he would bring the land to be sailed on and the sea to be traveled over, because of the haughtiness of his mind.
verses.5:22: He also left governors to afflict the nation: in Jerusalem, Philip, a Phrygian by birth, more cruel in character than the very one by whom he was appointed;
verses.5:23: and at Gerizim, Andronicus and Menelaus, who pressed upon the citizens more severely than the rest.
verses.5:24: And since he was set against the Jews, he sent the hateful commander Apollonius with an army of twenty-two thousand, commanding him to kill all of full age and to sell the women and youths.
verses.5:25: When he had come to Jerusalem, pretending peace, he remained quiet until the holy day of the Sabbath; and then, while the Jews were keeping the day of rest, he commanded his men to take up arms.
verses.5:26: And he slaughtered all who had come out to the spectacle; and rushing through the city with armed men, he put to death a huge multitude.
verses.5:27: But Judas Maccabeus, who had been the tenth, had withdrawn into a deserted place, and there he passed his life among wild beasts in the mountains with his men; and feeding on grass for food, they remained there, so that they might not be sharers in the defilement.
verses.6:1: But not long afterward, the king sent a certain old man from Antioch to compel the Jews to depart from the ancestral laws and the laws of God,
verses.6:2: and also to defile the temple that was in Jerusalem and to name it after Olympian Jupiter, and the one on Gerizim, according to what those who inhabited the place were, after Hospitable Jupiter.
verses.6:3: Now the onslaught of evils was extremely severe and grievous to all:
verses.6:4: for the temple was full of debauchery and revelries of the Gentiles, and of men fornicating with prostitutes; and into the sacred buildings women thrust themselves of their own accord, bringing inside things that were not lawful.
verses.6:5: The altar also was full of unlawful things that were forbidden by the laws.
verses.6:6: Moreover, neither were the Sabbaths kept, nor were the ancestral festival days observed, nor did anyone simply confess himself to be a Jew.
verses.6:7: And they were led with bitter compulsion on the king's birthday to the sacrifices; and when the sacred rites of Liber were celebrated, they were forced, crowned with ivy, to walk in procession for Liber.
verses.6:8: Moreover, a decree went out to the neighboring cities of the Gentiles, at the suggestion of the people of Ptolemais, that they themselves should also act in the same way against the Jews, so that they would offer sacrifice,
verses.6:9: and should kill those who were unwilling to go over to the customs of the Gentiles. So misery was there to be seen.
verses.6:10: For two women were denounced for having circumcised their children; and after they had led the women around publicly through the city with the infants hung at their breasts, they hurled them headlong over the walls.
verses.6:11: Others, however, assembling in nearby caves and secretly celebrating the Sabbath day, when they had been reported to Philip, were burned with flames, because they feared, on account of religion and observance, to bring aid to themselves by hand.
verses.6:12: Now I implore those who are about to read this book not to recoil because of adverse events, but to consider that the things that happened were not for the destruction, but for the discipline of our race.
verses.6:13: For indeed, not to allow sinners for a long time to act as they please, but immediately to inflict punishments, is a sign of great kindness.
verses.6:14: For not as with other nations, where the Lord waits patiently so that when the day of judgment arrives He may punish them in the fullness of their sins,
verses.6:15: has He likewise determined in our case, that once our sins have come to their end, only then should He take vengeance on us.
verses.6:16: Therefore He indeed never removes His mercy from us; yet while disciplining in adversities, He has not abandoned His people.
verses.6:17: But let these things be said by us in few words as a reminder to the readers. For now we must come to the narrative.
verses.6:18: Therefore Eleazar, one of the foremost scribes, a man advanced in age and noble in countenance, with his mouth opened and gaping, was compelled to eat pork.
verses.6:19: But he, embracing a most glorious death rather than a loathsome life, went forward voluntarily to torture.
verses.6:20: And considering how he ought to come forward, enduring patiently, he resolved not to admit unlawful things out of love for life.
verses.6:21: But those who stood by, moved by unjust pity because of their longstanding friendship with the man, took him aside privately and urged that meats be brought that were lawful for him to eat, so that he might pretend to have eaten from the meats of the sacrifice, as the king had commanded,
verses.6:22: so that by doing this he might be delivered from death; and because of their old friendship with the man, they showed him this kindness.
verses.6:23: But he began to consider the worthy eminence of his age and old age, and the gray hair of his inborn nobility, and the deeds of his most excellent way of life from boyhood; and in accordance with the ordinances of the holy law established by God, he answered quickly, saying that he wished to be sent ahead into the underworld.
verses.6:24: "For it is not worthy of our age," he said, "to pretend, so that many of the young men, supposing that Eleazar at ninety years of age has gone over to the way of life of foreigners,
verses.6:25: should themselves be deceived because of my pretense and because of a short span of perishable life, and through this I should bring stain and detestation upon my old age.
verses.6:26: For even if at the present time I should be rescued from the tortures of men, yet neither alive nor dead will I escape the hand of the Almighty.
verses.6:27: Therefore, by departing from life courageously, I will indeed show myself worthy of old age,
verses.6:28: and I will leave a courageous example to the young men, if with a ready spirit and courageously I undergo an honorable death for the most solemn and most holy laws." When these things had been said, he was immediately dragged to torture.
verses.6:29: Now those who were leading him, and who a little while before had been gentler, were turned to anger because of the words spoken by him, which they supposed had been uttered out of arrogance.
verses.6:30: But as he was being put to death by blows, he groaned and said, "Lord, You who have holy knowledge, You clearly know that although I could be delivered from death, I endure severe pains of the body; yet in my soul, out of fear of You, I gladly suffer these things."
verses.6:31: And indeed this man departed from life in this way, leaving behind not only to the young men, but also to the entire nation, the memory of his death as an example of virtue and courage.
verses.7:1: Now it also happened that seven brothers, together with their mother, were seized and compelled by the king to eat pork contrary to divine law, being tormented with whips and bull-hide thongs.
verses.7:2: And one of them, who was the first, spoke thus: "What are you asking, and what do you want to learn from us? We are ready to die rather than transgress the ancestral laws of God."
verses.7:3: Therefore the king, enraged, ordered bronze pans and cauldrons to be heated; and when these were immediately heated,
verses.7:4: he ordered the tongue of the one who had spoken first to be cut out, and after the skin of his head had been torn off, the extremities of his hands and feet also to be severed, while the rest of his brothers and his mother looked on.
verses.7:5: And when he had now been rendered helpless in every way, he ordered fire to be brought near and for him, while still breathing, to be roasted in the pan; and while he was tormented in it for a long time, the rest, together with their mother, encouraged one another to die courageously,
verses.7:6: saying, "The Lord God will look upon the truth and will take comfort in us, just as Moses declared in the testimony of the song: 'And in His servants He will take comfort.'"
verses.7:7: Therefore, when that first one had died in this way, they led the next one forward to be mocked; and after the skin of his head had been torn off along with the hair, they asked whether he would eat before he was punished throughout his whole body, limb by limb.
verses.7:8: But he, answering in the ancestral language, said, "I will not do it." Because of this, he too, next in order, underwent the tortures of the first;
verses.7:9: and at his last breath, he spoke thus: "You indeed, most wicked one, destroy us in the present life; but the King of the world will raise us who have died for His laws in the resurrection of eternal life."
verses.7:10: After him the third was mocked; and when asked for his tongue, he quickly put it out and steadfastly stretched out his hands,
verses.7:11: and with confidence he said, "From heaven I possess these, but because of the laws of God I now despise these very things, since I hope to receive them back from Him,"
verses.7:12: so that the king and those who were with him marveled at the spirit of the young man, because he regarded the torments as nothing.
verses.7:13: And when this one had died in this way, they mistreated the fourth, torturing him in the same manner.
verses.7:14: And when he was now at the point of death, he spoke thus: "It is better for those given over to death by men to await hope from God, to be raised up again by Him; for to you there will be no resurrection to life."
verses.7:15: And when they had brought the fifth forward, they mistreated him. But he, looking at him,
verses.7:16: said, "Having power among men, though you are perishable, you do what you want; yet do not think that our race has been abandoned by God;
verses.7:17: but you, wait patiently, and you will see His great power, how He will torture you and your seed."
verses.7:18: After him they led out the sixth, and as he was beginning to die, he spoke thus: "Do not be mistaken in vain; for we suffer these things because of ourselves, sinning against our God, and things worthy of wonder have happened among us;
verses.7:19: but do not suppose that it will go unpunished for you because you have attempted to fight against God."
verses.7:20: Now the mother was admirable beyond measure and worthy of the remembrance of the good, who, seeing her seven sons perishing within the span of a single day, bore it with good courage because of the hope that she had in God;
verses.7:21: she encouraged each of them courageously in the ancestral language, filled with wisdom; and infusing a manly spirit into her womanly thought,
verses.7:22: she said to them, "I do not know how you appeared in my womb; for neither did I grant you spirit and soul and life, nor did I myself fit together the limbs of each of you;
verses.7:23: rather, the Creator of the world, who formed the birth of man and who devised the origin of all things, will give back to you again with mercy both spirit and life, just as now you despise yourselves because of His laws."
verses.7:24: Now Antiochus, supposing that he was being held in contempt, and at the same time disdaining the voice of the one reproaching him, since the youngest still remained, not only urged him with words but also affirmed with an oath that he would make him rich and fortunate, would hold him as a friend once turned away from the ancestral laws, and would provide him with the necessary things.
verses.7:25: But when the young man was in no way inclined toward these things, the king called the mother and urged her to become the young man's deliverance.
verses.7:26: And when he had urged her with many words, she promised that she would persuade her son.
verses.7:27: Therefore, leaning toward him and mocking the cruel tyrant, she spoke in the ancestral language: "My son, have mercy on me, who carried you in the womb for nine months, and gave you milk for three years and nourished you, and brought you up to this age.
verses.7:28: I implore you, child, to look at heaven and earth, and at all things that are in them, and to understand that God made them and the human race from nothing;
verses.7:29: thus it will come about that you will not fear this executioner, but having become a partner worthy of your brothers, accept death, so that in that mercy I may receive you back with your brothers."
verses.7:30: While she was still saying these things, the young man said, "Whom are you waiting for? I do not obey the command of the king, but the command of the law that was given to us through Moses.
verses.7:31: But you, who have become the inventor of all wickedness against the Hebrews, will not escape the hand of God.
verses.7:32: For we suffer these things for our sins.
verses.7:33: And even if the Lord our God has been angry with us for a little while for the sake of rebuke and correction, yet He will again be reconciled to His servants.
verses.7:34: But you, wicked one and most vile of all men, do not be lifted up in vain with empty hopes, inflamed against His servants;
verses.7:35: for you have not yet escaped the judgment of Almighty God, who observes all things.
verses.7:36: For my brothers, having now endured a brief pain, have come under the covenant of eternal life; but you, by the judgment of God, will pay the just penalties of your arrogance.
verses.7:37: And I, like my brothers, surrender my soul and my body for the ancestral laws, calling upon God to become merciful to our nation quickly, and that with tortures and beatings you may confess that He alone is God.
verses.7:38: But in me and in my brothers, the wrath of the Almighty, which has been justly brought upon our entire race, will cease."
verses.7:39: Then the king, inflamed with anger against him, vented his rage more cruelly than against all the others, indignant that he had been mocked.
verses.7:40: And so this one also died pure, trusting in the Lord in all things.
verses.7:41: And last of all, after her sons, the mother also met her end.
verses.7:42: Therefore, concerning the sacrifices and the extreme cruelties, enough has been said.
verses.8:1: Now Judas Maccabeus and those who were with him were secretly entering the villages, and calling together their relatives and friends, and taking in those who remained in Judaism, they led out to themselves six thousand men.
verses.8:2: And they called upon the Lord that He would look upon the people who were being trampled down by all, and have mercy on the temple that was being defiled by the ungodly;
verses.8:3: that He would also have mercy on the destruction of the city that was about to be leveled at once, and hear the voice of the blood crying out to Him;
verses.8:4: and that He would also remember the most unjust deaths of the innocent little children, and the blasphemies directed against His name, and be indignant over these things.
verses.8:5: But Maccabeus, once a multitude had been gathered together, was becoming unbearable to the nations, for the wrath of the Lord was turned into mercy.
verses.8:6: And coming unexpectedly upon villages and cities, he set them on fire, and seizing advantageous places, he inflicted not a few slaughters upon the enemies.
verses.8:7: Moreover, he set out especially by night for raids of this kind, and the report of his valor was spreading everywhere.
verses.8:8: Now Philip, seeing that the man was gradually coming to advancement and that affairs were more frequently turning out swiftly for him, wrote to Ptolemy, the commander of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, that he should bring aid to the king's affairs.
verses.8:9: And he quickly sent Nicanor, son of Patroclus, one of the foremost friends, having given him no fewer than twenty thousand armed men from the mixed nations, to destroy the entire race of the Jews, with Gorgias joined to him, a military man and most experienced in matters of war.
verses.8:10: Now Nicanor resolved to make up for the king, from the captivity of the Jews, the tribute of two thousand talents that was to be given to the Romans.
verses.8:11: And immediately he sent to the coastal cities, calling them to the purchase of Jewish slaves, promising that he would sell off ninety slaves for a talent, having no regard for the vengeance that was about to overtake him from the Almighty.
verses.8:12: Now when Judas found out, he made known Nicanor's coming to the Jews who were with him.
verses.8:13: Some of them, being afraid and not believing in the justice of God, turned to flight.
verses.8:14: Others, however, sold whatever remained to them, and at the same time pleaded with the Lord that He would rescue them from the ungodly Nicanor, who had sold them before he came to close quarters,
verses.8:15: if not for their sake, yet for the sake of the covenant that was with their fathers, and for the sake of the invocation of His holy and magnificent name upon them.
verses.8:16: Now Maccabeus, having called together the seven thousand who were with him, urged them not to be reconciled to the enemies, nor to fear the multitude of enemies coming unjustly against them, but to fight bravely,
verses.8:17: keeping before their eyes the outrage that had been unjustly inflicted upon the holy place by them, and likewise the wrong done to the city held in mockery, and furthermore the overturned institutions of the ancients.
verses.8:18: "For they indeed trust in weapons," he said, "and in boldness at the same time; but we trust in the Almighty Lord, who is able with a single nod to destroy both those coming against us and the entire world."
verses.8:19: Moreover, he also reminded them of the acts of aid from God that were performed for their ancestors, and how under Sennacherib one hundred eighty-five thousand perished,
verses.8:20: and of the battle that they had against the Galatians in Babylonia: how when it came to the engagement, while their Macedonian allies hesitated, all of them, six thousand alone, killed one hundred twenty thousand because of the help given to them from heaven, and obtained very many rewards for these things.
verses.8:21: By these words they were made steadfast, and ready to die for the laws and their homeland.
verses.8:22: Therefore he appointed his brothers as commanders for each division—Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan—placing one thousand five hundred under each one.
verses.8:23: In addition to this, after the holy book had been read to them by Ezra, and after the watchword of God's help had been given, he himself, as commander in the front line, engaged in battle with Nicanor.
verses.8:24: And with the Almighty having become their helper, they killed more than nine thousand men, and they forced the greater part of Nicanor's army, disabled by wounds, to flee.
verses.8:25: And having carried off the money of those who had come to purchase them, they pursued them in every direction;
verses.8:26: but they turned back, constrained by the hour, for it was before the Sabbath; for this reason they did not persist in pursuing them.
verses.8:27: Now gathering their weapons and spoils, they observed the Sabbath, blessing the Lord, who delivered them on that day, distilling the beginning of mercy upon them.
verses.8:28: After the Sabbath, however, they divided the spoils among the disabled, the orphans, and the widows, and the remainder they themselves kept along with their own people.
verses.8:29: Therefore, when these things had been done, and a supplication had been made in common by all, they implored the merciful Lord that He would be completely reconciled to His servants.
verses.8:30: And of those who were with Timothy and Bacchides fighting against them, they killed more than twenty thousand, and they captured high strongholds, and divided abundant plunder, making an equal share for the disabled, the orphans, and the widows, and also for the elderly.
verses.8:31: And when they had carefully collected their weapons, they stored them all in advantageous places, while the remaining spoils they brought to Jerusalem.
verses.8:32: And they killed Philarches, who was with Timothy, a wicked man who had afflicted the Jews in many ways.
verses.8:33: And while they were holding victory celebrations in Jerusalem, they burned the one who had burned the sacred gates, that is, Callisthenes, when he had fled into a certain dwelling, a fitting reward having been repaid to him for his ungodly deeds.
verses.8:34: Now the most villainous Nicanor, who had brought a thousand merchants for the sale of the Jews,
verses.8:35: having been humbled by the help of the Lord through those whom he had regarded as nothing, having laid aside his garment of glory and fleeing through the inland regions, came alone to Antioch, having attained the utmost misfortune over the destruction of his army.
verses.8:36: And he who had promised the Romans that he would pay back the tribute from the captivity of Jerusalem now proclaimed that the Jews had God as their protector, and that on account of Him they were invulnerable, because they followed the laws established by Him.
verses.9:1: At that same time, Antiochus was returning in disgrace from Persia.
verses.9:2: For he had entered the city that is called Persepolis, and attempted to plunder the temple and oppress the city; but as the multitude rushed together to arms, they were turned to flight, and so it happened that Antiochus returned shamefully after the flight.
verses.9:3: And when he had come near Ecbatana, he learned what had been done concerning Nicanor and Timothy.
verses.9:4: Carried away in anger, however, he supposed that he could turn back upon the Jews the wrong done by those who had put him to flight; and therefore he ordered his chariot to be driven on, making the journey without pause, while heavenly judgment was pressing hard upon him, because he had spoken so arrogantly that he would come to Jerusalem and make it a burial heap of the Jews.
verses.9:5: But the Lord God of Israel, who sees all things, struck him with an incurable and invisible blow. For as soon as he finished this very speech, a terrible pain of the bowels seized him, and bitter torments of his inner parts,
verses.9:6: and indeed quite justly, since he had tortured the bowels of others with many and new tortures, although he in no way ceased from his malice.
verses.9:7: Moreover, filled with pride beyond this, breathing fire in his spirit against the Jews, and commanding the matter to be hastened, it happened that as he rushed along at full speed he fell from the chariot, and his limbs were racked by a severe impact of his body.
verses.9:8: And he who imagined himself to command even the waves of the sea, filled with pride beyond human measure, and to weigh the heights of the mountains on a balance, now brought low to the ground, was being carried in a litter, bearing witness in himself to the manifest power of God;
verses.9:9: so that worms swarmed out from the body of the ungodly man, and while he lived in pains his flesh fell away, and the army too was weighed down by his smell and stench;
verses.9:10: and the man who a little while before thought that he could touch the stars of heaven, no one could carry him because of the unbearable stench.
verses.9:11: From this point, therefore, brought down from his heavy pride, he began to come to a recognition of himself, warned by the divine blow, as his pains increased at every single moment.
verses.9:12: And when not even he himself could bear his own stench any longer, he spoke thus: "It is right to be subject to God, and for a mortal not to think as if equal to God."
verses.9:13: Now this wicked man prayed to the Lord, from whom he was not going to obtain mercy.
verses.9:14: And the city toward which he was coming in haste to bring it down to the ground and make it a tomb of piled-up bodies, he now wishes to make free;
verses.9:15: and the Jews, whom he had said he would not consider worthy even of burial, but would hand over to be torn apart by birds and wild beasts and would wipe out along with their little children, he now promises that he will make equal to the Athenians;
verses.9:16: that he will also adorn with the finest gifts the holy temple, which he had previously plundered, and multiply the sacred vessels, and furnish from his own revenues the expenses pertaining to the sacrifices;
verses.9:17: and beyond these things, that he will also become a Jew, and travel through every place of the earth, and proclaim the power of God.
verses.9:18: But as his pains did not cease (for the just judgment of God had come upon him), giving up hope, he wrote to the Jews a letter in the manner of a supplication, containing these things:
verses.9:19: "To the most excellent Jewish citizens: warmest greeting, good health, and happiness, from Antiochus the king and the princes.
verses.9:20: If you are in good health, and your children also, and everything is according to your wish, we give the greatest thanks.
verses.9:21: And I, being in a state of illness, yet kindly mindful of you after returning from the regions of Persia, and having been seized by a severe illness, have considered it necessary to take care for the common welfare,
verses.9:22: not despairing of myself, but having great hope of escaping the illness.
verses.9:23: Bearing in mind, moreover, that my father also, at the times when he was leading an army in the upper regions, pointed out who would take up the rule after him,
verses.9:24: so that if anything adverse should happen, or anything difficult should be reported, those who were in the regions, knowing to whom the supreme charge of affairs had been left, would not be troubled;
verses.9:25: and in addition to this, considering how all the powerful men nearby and the neighbors are lying in wait for opportunities and awaiting the outcome, I have designated my son Antiochus as king, whom I often commended to many of you when returning to the upper kingdoms; and I have written to him what is appended below.
verses.9:26: Therefore I implore and ask you, mindful of the benefits shown publicly and privately, that each one preserve loyalty toward me and toward my son.
verses.9:27: For I am confident that he will act moderately and humanely, and following my purpose, will also be accommodating to you."
verses.9:28: So the murderer and blasphemer, most severely struck, just as he himself had treated others, ended his life by a miserable death in a foreign land in the mountains.
verses.9:29: Now Philip, his foster brother, was transporting the body; fearing the son of Antiochus, he departed into Egypt to Ptolemy Philometor.
verses.10:1: Now Maccabeus and those who were with him, with the Lord protecting them, recovered the temple and the city.
verses.10:2: However, he demolished the altars that the foreigners had built throughout the streets, and likewise the shrines.
verses.10:3: And after the temple was purified, they made another altar, and having kindled fire from fiery stones, they offered sacrifices after two years, and they set out incense, lamps, and the loaves of the presentation.
verses.10:4: When these things had been done, they pleaded with the Lord, prostrate on the ground, that they would not again fall into such evils, but also, if at any time they should sin, that they would be disciplined more gently by Him and not be handed over to barbarous and blasphemous men.
verses.10:5: Now on the day on which the temple had been defiled by the foreigners, it happened that on that same day the purification took place, on the twenty-fifth day of the month that was Chislev.
verses.10:6: And with joy they celebrated for eight days in the manner of Tabernacles, remembering that a short time before they had kept the solemn day of Tabernacles in the mountains and in caves like wild beasts.
verses.10:7: For this reason they carried wreathed staffs, green branches, and palms before Him who had granted success for His place to be cleansed.
verses.10:8: And they decreed by a common ordinance and decree for the entire nation of the Jews to observe these days every year.
verses.10:9: And indeed, the departure from life of Antiochus, who was called the Noble, took place in this way.
verses.10:10: Now, however, we will recount the things that occurred concerning Eupator, the son of the ungodly Antiochus, summarizing the evils that occurred in the wars.
verses.10:11: For he, having assumed the kingdom, appointed over the affairs of the kingdom a certain Lysias, commander of the army of Phoenicia and Syria.
verses.10:12: For Ptolemy, who was called Macer, resolved to hold fast to justice toward the Jews, and especially because of the injustice that had been done against them, and to deal peacefully with them.
verses.10:13: But because of this, he was accused by the friends before Eupator; and since he frequently heard himself called a traitor because he had abandoned Cyprus, which had been entrusted to him by Philometor, and having gone over to Antiochus the Noble had also withdrawn from him, he ended his life with poison.
verses.10:14: Now Gorgias, since he was commander of the districts, having taken on strangers, frequently waged war against the Jews.
verses.10:15: Moreover, the Jews who held the strategic fortresses were taking in those driven out from Jerusalem and attempting to wage war.
verses.10:16: But those who were with Maccabeus, pleading with the Lord through prayers that He would be a helper to them, launched an assault against the fortresses of the Idumeans.
verses.10:17: And pressing on with great force, they captured the places, killed those who came against them, and altogether slaughtered no fewer than twenty thousand.
verses.10:18: Now when certain men had fled into two strongly fortified towers, having all the equipment for fighting back,
verses.10:19: Maccabeus, having left behind for their capture Simon, Joseph, and also Zacchaeus, along with those who were with them in considerable numbers, himself turned to the battles that were more pressing.
verses.10:20: But those who were with Simon, led by greed, were persuaded with money by some who were in the towers; and having accepted seventy thousand didrachmas, they let some escape.
verses.10:21: Now when it was reported to Maccabeus what had been done, having assembled the leaders of the people, he charged that they had sold their brothers for money, having released their adversaries.
verses.10:22: Therefore he put to death these men who had become traitors, and immediately seized the two towers.
verses.10:23: And conducting everything successfully with weapons and hands, he killed more than twenty thousand in the two fortresses.
verses.10:24: But Timothy, who previously had been defeated by the Jews, having summoned an army of a foreign multitude and having gathered Asian cavalry, arrived as though about to capture Judea by arms.
verses.10:25: Now Maccabeus and those who were with him, as he approached, implored the Lord, sprinkling their heads with earth, having their waists wrapped in sackcloth,
verses.10:26: falling down at the base of the altar, that He would be gracious to them, but an enemy to their enemies, and oppose their adversaries, just as the law says.
verses.10:27: And so after the prayer, having taken up their weapons, advancing some distance from the city and drawing close to the enemy, they halted.
verses.10:28: Now at the first rising of the sun, both sides engaged in battle: the one side having, along with valor, the Lord as the guarantor of victory and prosperity, while the other side had passion as their leader in war.
verses.10:29: But when the battle was fierce, five men on horses appeared from heaven to the adversaries, splendid with golden bridles, providing leadership to the Jews.
verses.10:30: Two of them, holding Maccabeus in the middle, preserved him unharmed, surrounded by their armor, while against the adversaries they hurled missiles and thunderbolts; because of this, both confounded with blindness and filled with turmoil, they fell.
verses.10:31: And twenty thousand five hundred were killed, and six hundred horsemen.
verses.10:32: But Timothy fled to Gazara, a fortified stronghold, over which Chaereas was in command.
verses.10:33: Now Maccabeus and those who were with him, rejoicing, besieged the stronghold for four days.
verses.10:34: But those who were inside, trusting in the strength of the place, cursed beyond measure and hurled abominable words.
verses.10:35: But when the fifth day was dawning, twenty young men from those who were with Maccabeus, inflamed in spirit because of the blasphemy, bravely approached the wall, and advancing with fierce courage, they began to climb up.
verses.10:36: And others also, climbing up in the same way, undertook to set fire to the towers and gates and to burn those revilers themselves alive.
verses.10:37: Now after the stronghold had been laid waste for two continuous days, they put to death Timothy, who was found hiding himself in a certain place, and they killed his brother Chaereas and Apollophanes.
verses.10:38: When these things had been done, with hymns and thanksgivings they blessed the Lord, who did great things in Israel and gave victory to them.
verses.11:1: But a short time afterward, Lysias, the king's guardian and relative, and overseer of affairs, being greatly displeased over the things that had happened,
verses.11:2: having gathered eighty thousand and all the cavalry, was marching against the Jews, thinking that he would make the captured city a dwelling place for the Gentiles,
verses.11:3: and would hold the temple for monetary gain, like the other shrines of the Gentiles, and the priesthood for sale each year.
verses.11:4: In no way considering the power of God, but unbridled in mind, he trusted in the multitude of foot soldiers, and in the thousands of horsemen, and in the eighty elephants.
verses.11:5: Now having entered Judea and approaching Beth-zur, which was in a narrow place at a distance of five stadia from Jerusalem, he was assaulting that stronghold.
verses.11:6: And when Maccabeus and those who were with him learned that the strongholds were being assaulted, they and the whole crowd together pleaded with the Lord with weeping and tears, that He would send a good angel for the deliverance of Israel.
verses.11:7: And Maccabeus himself, having first taken up arms, urged the others to face danger together with him and to bring help to their brothers.
verses.11:8: And as they were advancing together with an eager spirit, there appeared at Jerusalem a horseman going ahead of them in bright white clothing and golden armor, brandishing a spear.
verses.11:9: Then all together they blessed the merciful Lord and grew strong in spirit, ready to penetrate not only men, but even the fiercest beasts and iron walls.
verses.11:10: Therefore they went forward eagerly, having a helper from heaven and the Lord showing mercy upon them.
verses.11:11: And rushing with force upon the enemies like lions, they struck down from among them eleven thousand foot soldiers and one thousand six hundred horsemen.
verses.11:12: And they put all of them to flight, and many of them escaped wounded and naked. Even Lysias himself escaped by fleeing shamefully.
verses.11:13: And because he was not senseless, considering within himself the loss that had happened to him, and understanding that the Hebrews were invincible, relying on the help of Almighty God, he sent to them,
verses.11:14: and promised that he would consent to all things that are just, and that he would compel the king to become a friend.
verses.11:15: Now Maccabeus agreed to the requests of Lysias, having regard for what was beneficial in all things; and whatever Maccabeus wrote to Lysias concerning the Jews, the king granted.
verses.11:16: For letters had been written to the Jews by Lysias to this effect: "Lysias to the people of the Jews, greetings.
verses.11:17: John and Absalom, who had been sent by you, delivering the written documents, requested that I fulfill the things that were indicated through them.
verses.11:18: Therefore, whatever could be brought before the king, I laid out; and what the situation permitted, he granted.
verses.11:19: Therefore, if you keep good faith in affairs, I will also try from now on that there may be a cause of good things for you.
verses.11:20: And concerning the rest of the matters point by point, I have instructed by word of mouth both those men and these who have been sent by me to confer with you.
verses.11:21: Fare well. In the one hundred forty-eighth year, on the twenty-fourth day of the month of Dioscorus."
verses.11:22: Now the king's letter contained these things: "King Antiochus to his brother Lysias, greetings.
verses.11:23: Since our father has been transferred among the gods, we, wishing that those who are in our kingdom live without disturbance and apply diligence to their own affairs,
verses.11:24: have heard that the Jews did not consent to my father that they be transferred to the practice of the Greeks, but wish to hold to their own way of life, and for that reason request from us that their own lawful customs be granted to them.
verses.11:25: Wishing therefore that this nation also be at peace, we have resolved and decided that the temple be restored to them, so that they may live according to the custom of their ancestors.
verses.11:26: Therefore you will do well if you send to them and give the right hand, so that, having come to know our will, they may be in good spirits and devote themselves to their own interests."
verses.11:27: And to the Jews, the king's letter was as follows: "King Antiochus to the senate of the Jews and to the rest of the Jews, greetings.
verses.11:28: If you are well, you are as we wish; and we ourselves are also doing well.
verses.11:29: Menelaus has come to us, saying that you wish to go down to your own people who are with us.
verses.11:30: Therefore, to those who come and go up to the thirtieth day of the month of Xanthicus, we give right hands of security,
verses.11:31: so that the Jews may use their own foods and laws, just as before, and that none of them may in any way suffer trouble concerning the things that were done through ignorance.
verses.11:32: And we have also sent Menelaus to speak to you.
verses.11:33: Farewell. In the one hundred forty-eighth year, on the fifteenth day of the month of Xanthicus."
verses.11:34: And the Romans also sent a letter to this effect: "Quintus Memmius and Titus Manilius, envoys of the Romans, to the people of the Jews, greetings.
verses.11:35: As for the things that Lysias, the king's kinsman, granted to you, we also have granted them.
verses.11:36: But concerning the things that he judged should be referred to the king, send someone immediately, conferring more carefully among yourselves, so that we may decide as is fitting for you; for we are going to Antioch.
verses.11:37: And therefore hurry to write back, so that we also may know what your will is.
verses.11:38: Fare well. In the one hundred forty-eighth year, on the fifteenth day of the month of Xanthicus."
verses.12:1: When these agreements had been made, Lysias proceeded to the king, while the Jews attended to agriculture.
verses.12:2: But those who had remained behind, Timothy, and Apollonius the son of Gennaeus, and also Hieronymus, and Demophon besides these, and Nicanor the Cypriarch, did not allow them to live in stillness and quiet.
verses.12:3: And the people of Joppa perpetrated a certain outrage of this kind: they asked the Jews with whom they lived to board the boats that they had prepared, with their wives and children, as though no hostility lay hidden between them.
verses.12:4: Therefore, according to the common decree of the city, while they themselves consented and for the sake of peace had no suspicion, when they had gone out into deep water, they drowned no fewer than two hundred.
verses.12:5: When Judas learned of this cruelty committed against the people of his own nation, he gave orders to the men who were with him; and having called upon God, the righteous Judge,
verses.12:6: he came against the murderers of his brothers, and set fire to the harbor at night, burned up the boats, and put to death with the sword those who had fled from the fire.
verses.12:7: And when he had done these things in this way, he departed as though about to return again and uproot all the people of Joppa.
verses.12:8: But when he learned that those who were in Jamnia also intended to act in the same way toward the Jews living with them,
verses.12:9: he came upon the people of Jamnia also by night and set fire to the harbor with the ships, so that the light of the fire appeared in Jerusalem from two hundred forty stadia away.
verses.12:10: When they had already gone nine stadia from there and were marching toward Timothy, Arabs engaged him in battle, five thousand men and five hundred horsemen.
verses.12:11: And when a fierce battle took place and by the help of God turned out favorably, the remaining Arabs, defeated, asked Judas for the right hand to be given to them, promising that they would give pastures and be helpful in other matters.
verses.12:12: And Judas, judging them truly useful in many respects, promised peace; and after right hands were received, they departed to their tents.
verses.12:13: He also attacked a certain strong city enclosed by bridges and walls, which was inhabited by crowds of mixed nations, whose name was Caspin.
verses.12:14: But those who were inside, trusting in the firmness of the walls and their supply of provisions, acted rather carelessly, provoking Judas with curses and blaspheming, and speaking what is not lawful.
verses.12:15: Maccabeus, however, having called upon the great Ruler of the world, who without battering rams and siege engines threw down Jericho in the days of Joshua, charged fiercely at the walls;
verses.12:16: and having captured the city through the will of the Lord, he carried out countless slaughters, so that the adjacent lake, two stadia in width, seemed to flow with the blood of those who were killed.
verses.12:17: From there they marched seven hundred fifty stadia and came to Charax, to the Jews who are called Tubians;
verses.12:18: and they did not capture Timothy in those places, and having accomplished nothing he had withdrawn, leaving a very strong garrison in a certain place.
verses.12:19: Now Dositheus and Sosipater, who were commanders with Maccabeus, killed those left by Timothy in the garrison, ten thousand men.
verses.12:20: But Maccabeus, having arranged six thousand around himself and organized them by cohorts, advanced against Timothy, who had with him one hundred twenty thousand foot soldiers and two thousand five hundred horsemen.
verses.12:21: When the arrival of Judas became known, Timothy sent ahead the women and children and the rest of the baggage to the stronghold that is called Carnion; for it was impregnable and difficult of access because of the narrowness of the terrain.
verses.12:22: And when the first cohort of Judas appeared, terror was struck into the enemies from the presence of God, who sees all things; and they were turned to flight one from another, so that they were cast down more by their own men and crippled by the blows of their own swords.
verses.12:23: And Judas pressed on fiercely, punishing the profane, and struck down thirty thousand men from among them.
verses.12:24: Timothy himself, however, fell among the forces of Dositheus and Sosipater, and with many pleas he begged to be released alive, because he held the parents and brothers of many of the Jews, who through his death might happen to be undone.
verses.12:25: And when he had given his word that he would restore them according to the agreement, they released him unharmed for the safety of their brothers.
verses.12:26: Then Judas marched out to Carnion, and twenty-five thousand were killed.
verses.12:27: After the flight and slaughter of these, he moved the army to Ephron, a fortified city, in which a multitude of diverse nations lived; and strong young men, taking their stand before the walls, fought back bravely; and in it there were many siege engines and a supply of missiles.
verses.12:28: But when they had called upon the Almighty, who by His power shatters the strength of enemies, they captured the city, and of those who were inside they struck down twenty-five thousand.
verses.12:29: From there they went away to the city of the Scythians, which was six hundred stadia away from Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: But as the Jews who were among the people of Scythopolis testified that they were treated kindly by them, and that even in times of misfortune they had dealt gently with them,
verses.12:31: giving thanks to them and urging them for the future also to be kind toward their nation, they came to Jerusalem as the solemn day of Weeks was approaching.
verses.12:32: And after Pentecost they went out against Gorgias, the governor of Idumea.
verses.12:33: And he came out with three thousand foot soldiers and four hundred horsemen.
verses.12:34: When they clashed, it happened that a few of the Jews fell.
verses.12:35: Now a certain Dositheus, a horseman of Bacenor's men, a brave man, had hold of Gorgias; and while he wanted to capture him alive, a certain horseman of the Thracians rushed upon him and severed his shoulder, and so Gorgias escaped to Maresha.
verses.12:36: But when those who were with Esdris had fought for a long time and were exhausted, Judas called upon the Lord to become helper and leader of the battle,
verses.12:37: and beginning in the ancestral language and raising a shout with hymns, he put the soldiers of Gorgias to flight.
verses.12:38: Then Judas, having gathered the army, came to the city of Adullam; and since the seventh day was arriving, having purified themselves according to custom, they kept the Sabbath in that same place.
verses.12:39: And on the following day Judas came with his men to take up the bodies of those who had been struck down and place them with their parents in the ancestral tombs.
verses.12:40: But under the tunics of those who had been killed they found some of the votive offerings of the idols that were at Jamnia, which the law forbids to the Jews; therefore it became evident to all that they had fallen for this reason.
verses.12:41: Therefore all blessed the righteous judgment of the Lord, who had made hidden things evident;
verses.12:42: and so, turning to prayer, they asked that the offense that had been committed be given over to oblivion. But the most valiant Judas urged the people to keep themselves without sin, seeing before their eyes what had happened because of the sins of those who were struck down.
verses.12:43: And having made a collection, he sent twelve thousand drachmas of silver to Jerusalem for a sacrifice to be offered for the sins of the dead, thinking rightly and devoutly about the resurrection
verses.12:44: (for if he were not hoping that those who had fallen would rise again, it would seem superfluous and vain to pray for the dead),
verses.12:45: and because he considered that those who had fallen asleep with godliness had the finest grace stored up.
verses.12:46: Therefore it is a holy and salutary thought to pray earnestly for the deceased, so that they may be released from sins.
verses.13:1: In the one hundred forty-ninth year, Judas learned that Antiochus Eupator was coming with a multitude against Judea,
verses.13:2: and with him Lysias, the guardian and overseer of affairs, having with him one hundred ten thousand foot soldiers, and five thousand horsemen, and twenty-two elephants, and three hundred chariots with scythes.
verses.13:3: Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great deceit appealed to Antiochus, not for the safety of his homeland, but hoping to be appointed to the leadership.
verses.13:4: But the King of kings roused the anger of Antiochus against the sinner; and when Lysias suggested that this man was the cause of all the evils, he ordered (as is their custom) that he be seized and put to death in that same place.
verses.13:5: Now in that same place there was a tower of fifty cubits, having a heap of ashes all around; this tower looked down over a sheer drop.
